title: Google To Spend $1bn To Establish New Campus In New York
text:
Home Economy Google To Spend $1bn To Establish New Campus In New York Google To Spend $1bn To Establish New Campus In New York December 17, 2018 Admin2 SundiataPost Economy 0 Google
Washington – Alphabet Inc’s (GOOGL.O) Google is investing more than 1 billion dollars to establish a new campus in New York, said Ruth Porat, the Chief Financial Officer of Alphabet and Google. This is to make it to become the second major technology company after Amazon to pick America’s financial capital to expand and create thousands of jobs.
The 1.7 million square-foot campus, called Google Hudson Square, will include leased property at Hudson Street and Washington Street, the company said in a blog post on Monday.
Google hopes to start moving into the building by 2022.
Google’s plans to invest outside its home base mirror those of other U.S. tech bigwigs such as Apple Inc (AAPL.O), which recently said it would spend 1 billion dollars to build a new campus in Austin, Texas.
The move to invest in prime real estate in the Westside of Manhattan also underscores the growing importance of New York as a hub for innovation and an incubator for technology companies.
“Our investment in New York is a huge part of our commitment to grow and invest in U.S. facilities, offices and jobs.’’
In fact, we’re growing faster outside the Bay Area than within it,” said Porat.
Amazon.com Inc (AMZN.O) said in November it would create more than 25,000 jobs in both New York and the Washington, D.C. area by opening massive new offices.
Google’s first New York office at 111 Eighth Avenue is one of the city’s largest buildings that it bought in 2010 for 1.77 billion dollars.
Earlier this year, the company announced a 2.4 billion dollars purchase of the Manhattan Chelsea Market.
It also has leased space on Pier 57 jutting into the Hudson, which will create a four-block campus. With investments in Google Chelsea and Google Hudson Square, the company said it would more than double the number of employees in New York over the next 10 years.
